nodes.description: In DFNB53, biallelic damaging COL11A2 variants impair alpha-2(XI) collagen function. Disruption of type XI collagen in the tectorial membrane is associated with profound hearing loss across all frequencies, although the exact effect of each reported allele on collagen abundance or assembly is not fully resolved.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of COL11A2 causes autosomal recessive non-syndromic hearing loss at the DFNB53 locus.
evidence.snippet: The P621T mutation of COL11A2 affects the Y position of the canonical -Gly-X-Y- repeat in collagens. It lies near the amino-terminus of the triple helical region and causes ARNSHL.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations confirm that COL11A2 is responsible for autosomal recessive non-syndromic hearing loss DFNB53.
evidence.snippet: The novel p.Ala37Ser is the first missense mutation located in the NC4 domain of the COL11A2 protein.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of COL11A2 causes autosomal recessive non-syndromic hearing loss at the DFNB53 locus.
evidence.snippet: This finding suggests that mutation type and location are critical determinants in defining the phenotype of COL11A2 associated diseases.

nodes.description: In DFNA13, heterozygous variants predicted to affect the collagen triple-helix domain disrupt COL11A2 function. Model-organism evidence links Col11a2 disruption to loss of organized collagen fibrils in the cochlear tectorial membrane, providing a structural route to the characteristic mid-frequency hearing loss.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in COL11A2 cause non-syndromic hearing loss (DFNA13).
evidence.snippet: Mice with a targeted disruption of Col11a2 also were shown to have hearing loss. Electron microscopy of the tectorial membrane of these mice revealed loss of organization of the collagen fibrils.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in COL11A2 cause non-syndromic hearing loss (DFNA13).
evidence.snippet: In both families, deafness is non-progressive and predominantly affects middle frequencies.

nodes.description: The characteristic audiometric pattern of DFNA13 is a non-progressive, prelingual sensorineural hearing loss that predominantly affects middle frequencies. This pattern likely reflects the frequency-specific mechanical properties of the tectorial membrane, which relies on collagen XI for its gradient of stiffness along the cochlear spiral.

evidence.snippet: All homozygous individuals in those families had early onset profound hearing loss across all frequencies without syndromic findings.

nodes.description: Sensorineural hearing loss is the defining feature of both DFNA13 and DFNB53. In DFNA13, hearing loss is non-progressive and predominantly affects mid-frequencies. In DFNB53, hearing loss is prelingual, severe-to-profound, and affects all frequencies.
